full_judgment: 3. Mr Md Ruhul Amin argues from the records that the petitioner has sought for pre-emption in respect of .51 acres of land of plot No. 749 under khatain No. 656 bearing a jama of Tk. 360 only. He submits that the pre-emptee opposite-parties are not co-sharers of the disputed Khatian No. 656. Plot No. 749 appertains to two holdings, namely, holding Nos. 656 comprises of 1.53 acres of land and plot No. 749 under holding No. 284 comprises of .51 acres of land. The pre-emptee-opposite-parties claimed to be co-sharers by purchase. Their predecessor purchased same lands from plot No. 749 but the purchases took place under khatain No. 284 bearing a jama of Tk. 6/00 only. Mr Ruhul Amin has referred to Exts. A and A(2), the documents of purchase of the opposite-parties, wherefrom it is clear that their predecessor purchased land from the disputed plot No. 749 but appertaining to holding No. 284. As the right of preemption accrues holding-wise, it cannot be said that the pre-emptee opposite-parties were co-sharer tenants in the holding No, 656 The Courts below clearly erred in law in refusing pre-emption on the ground of the pre-emptees being co sharer tenants of the holding in question. That concurrent finding is also reversed.
